newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down two at 962 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down two at 962 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 984 as of July 25, up 22 from the prior week and 210 above the year-ago total of 774, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 24 to 831, while rigs working offshore fell four to 125. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose two to 28.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Oklahoma, which was up by 16, Texas, which was up by 13, and Kansas, which was up by three.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count was down by four at 121.
A total of 398 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 17 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 5 to 583, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at three.
There were 223 rigs drilling directionally, 66 drilling horizontally and 665 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 11 to 395, versus 292 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
